query: My deep model runs out of GPU room for intermediate results; I can spend extra compute but have almost no spare host RAM.
I have lots of idle host RAM but can't afford any recomputation; how can the card keep fewer saved intermediate results?
With bf16 on an A100, do I still need the utility that multiplies the loss before the backward pass?
How do I train small extra matrices on a 4-bit-stored 7B model on a 16 GB card, and which loading options does that need?
Which settings pick the layers that get the small trainable add-on matrices, and enable the size-and-direction variant?
Every one of my 8 GPUs keeps a full copy of weights, updates and optimizer state; how can they split it instead of duplicating?
Inside a single layer the weight matrix is too big for one GPU; how can several GPUs share that one multiplication?
Our chat server reserves worst-case room per request for stored keys and values; how can that be handed out in small pieces on demand?
Rule of thumb for how much of the card's RAM an inference server should claim up front?
Which parameters set the group size and zero-point when 4-bit rounding relies on rescaling salient input channels instead of layer-by-layer error correction?
How many samples should go into each weight update when only a few fit on my card at once, and how do I still reach that number?
Why do half-width number formats let training use less room and run faster while the weight updates stay accurate?
Walk me through the whole process of teaching a 7B chat model new behaviour from example conversations on one 16 GB card.
What's a sensible starting width for the trainable add-on matrices, and how large a multiplier should their output get?
Our training job spans several machines and hangs at start-up while the processes try to find each other; what must the network and launch environment provide?
Which option decides how the network is cut into separately handled units when its weights are spread over devices, and which strategy controls what stays replicated?
Short requests finish early and leave the card idle while one long request in the same group keeps running; how can finished slots be refilled immediately?
Can a tiny helper that guesses several next words at once, checked by the big model in one pass, speed up generation without changing its output?
How can a much smaller network be trained to imitate a large one's output probabilities instead of learning from the raw labels?
How can weights be rounded to 4 bits one layer at a time while compensating each layer's rounding error using a small sample of inputs?
